run.question:
Alertmanager alert HighRequestErrorRate (severity critical) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-26T04:49:59Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The HighRequestErrorRate alert for frontend is firing because the frontend's checkout path is failing: at 04:52:59 its only error spans were POST /api/checkout (1.44/s), oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder (0.72/s) and executing api route /api/checkout (0.72/s), and the frontend pod logs show '14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.208.149:8080' on the placeOrder call, 10.96.208.149 being the clusterIP of Service checkout, whose Endpoints object has no addresses. The checkout pod cannot start: Deployment checkout's container image was changed (last write by manager OpenAPI-Generator at 04:48:31) from ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout to quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6..., which does not exist, so the new pod is Pending with ImagePullBackOff and the old pod was scaled down at 04:48:32. POST /api/checkout succeeded at ~1.49/s up to 04:48 and turned to errors (0.42/s at 04:50 rising to 1.44/s at 04:53). A simultaneous, separate change to Deployment recommendation and ConfigMap recommendation-config (malformed JSON config causing the new pod's init container to crash-loop) did not break recommendation: the Deployment kept a ready replica, its Service still had an endpoint, and frontend's ListRecommendations error rate was 0. Note the rule's annotation says 'above 3' while its expression compares > 0, so the alert fires at 2.91. Metric history for these series starts around 04:44 and the whole otel-demo namespace was (re)deployed at 04:41:07, so no long pre-incident baseline exists.

claims.text: The firing alert is the rule HighRequestErrorRate in rule group opentelemetrydemo.frontend.goldensignal, expression sum by (service_name, namespace) (rate(traces_span_metrics_calls_total{namespace="otel-demo",service_name=~"frontend|frontend-proxy",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}[2m])) > 0; the frontend alert is firing with value 2.9111111111111105 and activeAt 2026-11-26T04:49:59Z, and the same group also has frontend-proxy firing with value 1.422222222222222, while the rule annotation text says the error rate is 'above 3'.

At the 04:52:59 evaluation the frontend error-span rate was concentrated entirely on the checkout path: POST /api/checkout 1.4444444444444442/s, oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder 0.7222222222222221/s, executing api route (pages) /api/checkout 0.7222222222222221/s and tcp.connect 0.02222222222222222/s; frontend-proxy showed POST 0.711111111111111/s and router frontend egress 0.711111111111111/s.

Frontend span POST /api/checkout was succeeding before the change and failing after it: STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate 1.4888888888888887/s at 04:48, 1.4666666666666666/s at 04:49, 0.9555555555555555/s at 04:50, 0.2/s at 04:51 and 0 at 04:52 and 04:53, while STATUS_CODE_ERROR rate was 0 at 04:46-04:49, then 0.4222222222222222/s at 04:50, 1.222222222222222/s at 04:51, 1.5555555555555554/s at 04:52 and 1.4444444444444442/s at 04:53 (returned series begin at source_start_at 04:44).

Frontend pod logs (container frontend, pod frontend-5c847cc9bd-9dfr6) contain repeated errors in the placeOrder code path between 04:51:26Z and 04:52:11Z with the exact message "14 UNAVAILABLE: No connection established. Last error: Error: connect ECONNREFUSED 10.96.208.149:8080. Resolution note: " and stack frames at ServiceClientImpl.makeUnaryRequest / clientMethodTrace [as placeOrder].

Service checkout has clusterIP 10.96.208.149, port 8080 and selector opentelemetry.io/name=checkout; pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-p6cbb carries label opentelemetry.io/name=checkout, so the Service selector matches the new pod. The checkout Endpoints object lists port 8080 but no addresses, whereas other otel-demo services return addresses.

Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo currently declares one container named checkout with image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a; its managedFieldsSummary shows helm Apply at 04:41:07Z and an Update by manager "OpenAPI-Generator" at 04:48:31Z, observedGeneration 4, and status condition Available=False reason MinimumReplicasUnavailable at 04:48:38Z with ready and available replicas null.

ReplicaSet checkout-64c65899fc (created 04:41:07Z) used container image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout, while ReplicaSet checkout-7ffc7768f4 (created 04:48:31Z) uses quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6ce98bea7470d39364356ec0a8482fa7356ac92e132256539417688da615a.

Events for namespace otel-demo: Deployment checkout scaled replica set checkout-64c65899fc from 1 to 0 and checkout-7ffc7768f4 up at 04:48:32Z; pod checkout-64c65899fc-dc9mx was killed at 04:48:32Z; pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-hxqq7 recorded Failed/ErrImagePull at 04:48:32Z for image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64@sha256:20c6... with 'not found'; pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-p6cbb recorded BackOff pulling that image (count 16) and Failed/ImagePullBackOff (count 15) by 04:52:49Z.

Pod checkout-7ffc7768f4-p6cbb is in phase Pending with container checkout waiting, reason ImagePullBackOff, message 'Back-off pulling image "quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6...": ErrImagePull: ... not found', restartCount 0; its init container wait-for-kafka (busybox) terminated Completed with exit code 0 and its Ready condition is False with reason ContainersNotReady.

Deployment checkout's replacement image quay.io/it-bench/hello-bench-arm64:2.0.0@sha256:20c6... does not exist, so the only checkout pod never starts and the checkout Service has no ready endpoints; this is what the frontend reports as ECONNREFUSED to 10.96.208.149:8080 and what drives the frontend and frontend-proxy error-span rates, so Deployment checkout in namespace otel-demo is the object where this fault originates.

Deployment recommendation and ConfigMap recommendation-config were also updated at 04:48:30Z by manager "OpenAPI-Generator"; the resulting new pod recommendation-59897fb7d5-f2l7p has init container worker (image registry.access.redhat.com/ubi10/python-314-minimal:...) in CrashLoopBackOff with restartCount 5 and last terminated state exit code 1 reason Error, so its recommendation container is still PodInitializing, while the Deployment reports ready 1 and available 1 and Service recommendation still has address 10.244.2.117:8080.

ConfigMap recommendation-config holds data key config with the invalid JSON text '{"configuration_items": [{"name": fake}]}' (unquoted value) and data key script whose code loads ~/config/config.json with json.load and calls sys.exit(1) on json.JSONDecodeError.
No NetworkPolicy objects and no ResourceQuota objects exist in namespace otel-demo at query time.

In the ten-minute window ending 04:50 the per-service error-span increase was frontend 210.60300512820515 and frontend-proxy 83.8114, and that result contained no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series for ad, cart, payment, shipping, currency, email, product-catalog, quote, kafka or checkout.

Frontend operations outside the checkout path were not erroring at 04:52:59: GET /api/data, GET /api/products/[productId]/index, GET /api/recommendations, GET /api/cart, oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, oteldemo.CartService/GetCart, oteldemo.ProductCatalogService/GetProduct and oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations all had error-span rate 0, so the alert is not explained by a general frontend fault or by dependency errors other than checkout.

Service-level misconfiguration and admission constraints are excluded for checkout: the checkout Service selector (opentelemetry.io/name=checkout) matches the new pod's labels so the empty Endpoints list is caused by the pod not being ready, and no NetworkPolicy or ResourceQuota exists in the namespace.

The simultaneous recommendation change (ConfigMap recommendation-config with invalid JSON plus a new recommendation pod whose init container worker crash-loops) is rejected as the cause of this alert: recommendation kept a ready replica and an addressable Service endpoint, and frontend's oteldemo.RecommendationService/ListRecommendations error rate was 0 at 04:52:59, while the frontend error rise is confined to the checkout path.

Because the rule expression compares the error-span rate to > 0 rather than to the '3' written in its annotation, the alert fires on any sustained frontend/frontend-proxy error activity, including the present 2.911 value; if the intended threshold is 3, the rule should be corrected, and if not, the annotation is misleading.

Restore Deployment checkout's container image to the previous ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:3.1.0-checkout value (or roll back the 04:48:31Z spec change) so a checkout pod can start and the checkout Service endpoints repopulate, then confirm POST /api/checkout error spans return to zero.

Separately review the 04:48:30Z recommendation rollout: fix the invalid JSON in ConfigMap recommendation-config data key config so the worker init container can succeed and the pending recommendation pod can start.

Use Kubernetes audit logs (change_history is not integrated in this Run) to identify who or what acts as managedFields manager "OpenAPI-Generator", which updated Deployment checkout, Deployment recommendation and ConfigMap recommendation-config within one minute at 04:48:30-04:48:31Z.

gaps: The change_history integration is not available in this Run, so the actor, mechanism and intent behind manager "OpenAPI-Generator" and the 04:48:31Z image replacement on Deployment checkout could not be observed; managedFieldsSummary gives only the last write time, not the changed fields or earlier writes.

No pre-incident baseline exists for the frontend error series: the metric query for frontend error spans returned samples only from source_start_at 04:44Z, and all otel-demo pods and ReplicaSets were created by helm Apply at 04:41:07Z, so the sampled comparison relies on 04:44-04:49 (zero checkout errors) versus 04:50-04:53.
The old checkout pod checkout-64c65899fc-dc9mx was deleted at 04:48:32Z, so its application logs could not be read; only the new pod's status/events are available.

Jaeger sampling did not surface an error-tagged frontend span for the checkout call (a tags search on error=true returned nothing and the sampled traces covered ads/data traffic), so the span-level error detail is available only from the metrics status_code and the pod logs, not from trace status tags.
next_steps: Roll back the checkout Deployment image change and verify the checkout Service endpoints and POST /api/checkout success rate recover.
Correct the HighRequestErrorRate rule so its expression matches the documented 'above 3' threshold, or update the annotation if > 0 is intended.
Review Kubernetes audit logs for the principal behind the "OpenAPI-Generator" managedFields manager and for any other objects it modified in namespace otel-demo.
Repair the recommendation-config JSON so the recommendation rollout's worker init container can complete.

view.series_note: traces_span_metrics_calls_total counts spans of every operation of the service (internal, client and server spans alike), summed over the labels kept in this query; it is not a count of requests. status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET means the span carried no status; it does not mean the call succeeded.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). <none> means the path reached no value in that object, not that the field is absent from the kind; a filtered table is not a full picture of the kind. When the API server returns zero objects of a kind other than events (every page read), the result is ok with total_items_processed 0: it proves only that there were no objects matching this kind, namespace and selectors at query time, not that none existed during the incident. Zero events, or a list your filter reduced to nothing, stays no_data. metadata.managedFieldsSummary gives each manager's last write time only: it is not a full change history (earlier writes by the same manager are gone) and it does not say which fields that write changed.

import json
import os
import sys

def main():
    try:
        with open(os.path.expanduser("~/config/config.json"), "r") as f:
            data = json.load(f)

        items_count = len(data.get("configuration_items", []))

        print(f"Config loaded successfully with {items_count} configuration items")
        sys.exit(0)
    except json.JSONDecodeError as e:
        print(f"FATAL: Failed to parse configuration file: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"FATAL: Unexpected error loading configuration: {e}")
        sys.exit(1)

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
